title: introduce-session-factory-compact-iterators-and-decorrelated-retry-hooks
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Reduce friction when creating session-backed clients in Go, provide a compact streaming iterator primitive that reduces allocation churn, and decouple token refresh retry timing from request retries. This PR introduces three ergonomics-focused pieces: 1) SessionFactory: a small constructor utility to create session-bound SDK clients with sensible defaults (context timeouts, default headers, and optional telemetry hooks). 2) CompactIterator: a lightweight streaming iterator for pull-style streams that avoids channel goroutine proliferation and exposes a simple Next()/Err()/Value() surface. 3) DecorrelatedRetryHook: an auth-focused retry hook that separates token-refresh backoff from request retry backoff to avoid synchronized token refresh storms on large fleets. The change is intentionally backward-compatible: none of the public client interfaces were removed; new helpers are additive and documented. Checklist: [x] Implement SessionFactory with tests and examples; [x] Add CompactIterator and unit tests covering edge cases; [x] Implement DecorrelatedRetryHook and integrate with existing auth middleware; [x] Add examples in README and small migration note; [x] Run full CI and address lint/test failures. Compatibility notes: consumers can opt into SessionFactory by calling session.NewFactory or continue to use existing constructors. CompactIterator is implemented as a small wrapper over existing streaming transport and provides an adapter function StreamToCompactIterator for easy adoption. DecorrelatedRetryHook defaults can be tuned via RetryConfig; default values match existing behavior except the retry jitter window is now decorrelated for auth calls only. Related: ENG-4523 (stream ergonomics), ENG-4631 (retry stability).
